lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 5 you learned about time zones. How many degrees of longitude make one hour? (15°.) Today: Russia, the largest country, with 11 time zones, its taiga and its tundra.

Russia is the largest country on Earth, about 17 million km², about a ninth of all the land. It stretches across two continents: the Ural Mountains divide European Russia in the west from Asian Russia, Siberia, in the east.

Russia is so wide that it has 11 time zones. When it is 12:00 in Kaliningrad, in the far west, it is 22:00 in Kamchatka, in the far east. More than 140 million people live in Russia, most of them in the west.

In the far north lies the tundra: too cold for trees, with ground that stays frozen all year, permafrost, under about two-thirds of Russia. In the short summer the top layer thaws, and reindeer graze on mosses and lichens.

South of it is the taiga, the largest forest on Earth, of pine, spruce and larch; Russia holds about a fifth of the world's forests. Further south are the grassy steppes, where much of Russia's wheat grows.

Siberia's winters are among the coldest anywhere: Oymyakon, a village of about 500 people, once reached −67.7 °C. Great rivers, the Ob, Yenisei and Lena, flow north to the Arctic Ocean. Lake Baikal, 1,642 m deep, is the world's deepest lake.

Across it all runs the Trans-Siberian Railway, built from 1891 to 1916: 9,289 km from Moscow to Vladivostok, a journey of about a week. Russia also has much oil, gas, timber and metal, and a long northern coast on the Arctic Ocean.

Try it in the world: lay a railway from one side of your world to the other. Put a station and a clock every so often, each set an hour later than the one before as you go east. Next: a fieldwork enquiry.

exercises.prompt: What is the largest country on Earth?
Which mountains divide European Russia from Asian Russia?
exercises.hint: Look for the line between Moscow and Yekaterinburg.
exercises.explain: The Ural Mountains: west of them is European Russia, and east of them is Asian Russia, Siberia.

exercises.prompt: Permafrost is ground that stays frozen all year.
exercises.explain: True: it lies under about two-thirds of Russia.

exercises.hint: Pine, spruce and larch grow there.
choices: a huge forest of conifer trees
exercises.explain: The largest forest on Earth, mostly conifers.

exercises.prompt: How many time zones does Russia have?
exercises.hint: From Kaliningrad UTC+2 to Kamchatka UTC+12.
exercises.explain: 11 time zones, from Kaliningrad at UTC+2 to Kamchatka at UTC+12.

exercises.prompt: Moscow keeps UTC+3 and Vladivostok UTC+10. How many hours ahead of Moscow is Vladivostok?
exercises.hint: Take the smaller UTC number from the bigger.

exercises.prompt: The Trans-Siberian Railway is 9,289 km long. A train covers about 1,300 km a day. To the nearest whole day, how many days does it take?
exercises.hint: Divide the distance by the km a day, then round.
The tundra is too cold for trees; the taiga is forest.
exercises.explain: Tundra: reindeer, permafrost, mosses. Taiga: pine and spruce, the largest forest, bears.

exercises.prompt: Why do Siberia's rivers flood in spring?
exercises.hint: Which way do the rivers flow, and where does ice melt first?
choices: the south thaws while ice still blocks the north
exercises.explain: They flow north: their southern parts thaw first, while ice still blocks the colder north, so the water spills over.

exercises.prompt: Match each place to a fact.
exercises.hint: A lake, a village, a river and a capital city.
exercises.explain: Baikal: deepest lake. Oymyakon: −67.7 °C. The Volga: Europe's longest river. Moscow: the capital.

exercises.prompt: When it is 09:00 in Moscow (UTC+3), what time is it in Kamchatka (UTC+12)?
exercises.hint: Find how many hours ahead Kamchatka is, then add.

exercises.prompt: Lake Baikal is 1,642 m deep. How much deeper is it than a lake 250 m deep?
exercises.hint: Take the smaller depth from the bigger one.

exercises.prompt: Most of Russia's people live in Siberia.
exercises.hint: Where are Moscow and St Petersburg?
exercises.explain: False: most live in the west, in European Russia.

exercises.prompt: Why do most of Russia's people live in the west?
exercises.hint: Compare the west with frozen Siberia.
choices: it has milder weather and better farmland
exercises.explain: The west has a milder climate and good farmland; much of Siberia is frozen forest and tundra.

exercises.prompt: Put these cities in order from west to east.
exercises.hint: Follow the railway on the map, from its start.
exercises.explain: Moscow 38° E, Yekaterinburg 61° E, Novosibirsk 83° E, Irkutsk 104° E, Vladivostok 132° E.
